review_comments.body:
I don't really think this is nessecary, this could be an example value to me. I know I've done this in my own repo (in a seperate module that is, on purpose), but you're sort-of breaching the idea behind the RFC42 `settings` option [^1].

> Since with this approach there will be no more hardcoded defaults and composability is not a problem anymore, there is not a big need to have NixOS options for every setting anymore. Traditionally this has lead to huge modules with dozens of options, each of them only for a single field in the configuration. Such modules are problematic because they're hard to write, review and maintain, are generally of lower quality, fill the option listing with noise and more.

[^1]: https://github.com/NixOS/rfcs/blob/master/rfcs/0042-config-option.md
To be clear, this should be kept as it can't be configured thru `settings`...
Thanks for pointing to this, I dropped these options.

IMO we should direct consumers to the actual documentation, not the git repo, but again, just nitpicking here.

```suggestion
      description = ''
        Settings to set in config.toml.

        ::: {.note}
        See the [git-pages documentation](https://git-pages.org/running-a-server/#configuration) on configuring the server.
        :::
      '';
```

reviews.body:
Nice port! Some comments, and the checklist seems to check out!

- [x] Has a NixOS VM test
- [x] Has a `meta.maintainers` attribute
- [x] Systemd-specific definitions are behind `optionalAttrs (options ? systemd)` to promote portability.
- [x] `_class = "service"`
- [x] Modular services provided through `passthru.services` must override the default of the package option using `finalAttrs.finalPackage`
- [x] Is the modular services infrastructure sufficient for this service? If one or more features are not covered, comment in https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/428084
- [x] Has been added to `nixos/modules/misc/documentation/modular-services.nix`
Good to me after squashing into a single commit :+1:
I don't personally use git-pages the server, but I have no objections.

Apologies for the late review, something personal got in the way.

A few remarks, do whatever you want with it. I hope I don't come across as harsh or unnecessarily nitpicky, as I think this generally already looks very nice. I only think the mkdir call (and with it the default storage directory, and the working directory definition) should really be improved, so I am still requesting changes instead of approval with comments.
